Discussed architecture, compatibility, KV cache, quantization, monitoring and SOC2/VPC requirements. Agreed to run a benchmark in a trial Dedicated cluster and exchange security docs.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Sam Chen (Redwood SE), Jordan Patel (Head of ML, LatticeAI), Priya Nair (Product PM), Carlos Gomez (Platform Eng)

Auto-generated summary (may be rough): Discussed migration from OpenAI to Redwood Dedicated/Private, concerns about eval parity with vLLM/TGI and Anthropic models, infra integration (VPC/KMS/SSO), and next steps for pricing and benchmark.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining im we'll kick off, I'm Alex from Redwood, this is Sam our Solutions Engineer. Can you do quick intros?
[00:10] Jordan (LatticeAI): Yeah I'm Jordan, head of ML, we own model infra and quality.
[00:15] Priya (LatticeAI): Priya, product, owning roadmap and timelines.
[00:18] Carlos (LatticeAI): Carlos, platform, infra and security.
[00:22] Alex (AE): Great. The goal today is to understand your current stack, what's driving the migration from OpenAI, and see whether Dedicated or Private makes sense. Sam will dig into performance and compatibility later.
[00:33] Jordan: Quick backdrop we've been on OpenAI for last 18 months for chat completions and embeddings. Volume's grown, costs spiked, and latency is inconsistent for longer context chats. We're also evaluating running some on-prem variants with vLLM and TGI for cost control.
[00:48] Sam (SE): Thanks. When you say latency inconsistent, can you quantify p95 or tail latency?
[00:53] Jordan: p95 for short prompts around 300ms but for multi-turn with 4k context jumps to 1.4s and sometimes spikes to 3s. For embeddings p95 is about 350ms but throughput is a bottleneck during nightly batch jobs.
[01:10] Priya: Another driver is compliance we handle sensitive HR data and want encryption at rest, audit logs, and a VPC option. SOC 2 is table stakes.
[01:20] Alex (AE): Understood. Redwood Dedicated and Private both support VPC and KMS integration; we have SOC 2 reports we can share. For the latency and cost, many customers move to Dedicated to get predictable throughput and then optimize with batching, quantization, and KV caching.
[01:34] Carlos: We're also running some experiments with v-L-M folks write it as vLLM or V-L-M and TGI on self-hosted GPUs. The results are mixed; some prompt families degrade compared to OpenAI. Concern is eval parity can Redwood run the same model and match OpenAI/Anthropic outputs?
[01:52] Sam (SE): Good question. Compatibility depends on model and tokenizer parity. For open models that are identical, we can replicate weights and provide identical runtimes. Where customers see differences, it's often around sampling defaults, temperature or tokenizer mismatch, or custom logits processors. We also surface model variants in our catalog.
[02:08] Jordan: For us, eval parity is critical we have an automated eval harness with ~400 prompt tests. If outputs shift, product metrics drop.
[02:16] Alex (AE): Sounds like a POC where we run your eval suite against a Dedicated instance is the right next step.
[02:22] Priya: Timeline-wise we want something in staging in 4 weeks, production in 8-10 if results look good. Is that realistic?
[02:30] Sam (SE): Yes, for Dedicated a 4-week staging spin-up is common assuming no custom infra blockers. For Private on-prem it will be longer. Do you plan to store any PHI?
[02:40] Jordan: Not full PHI but sensitive HR records that might be regulated, so data residency and strict KMS controls matter.
[02:46] Carlos: On infra we use AWS in us-east-1, and have a VPC with strict egress policies. We'll need SAML SSO and RBAC for engineering teams.
[02:56] Alex (AE): Redwood Dedicated supports SAML/SSO and fine-grained RBAC; we can scope an audit log export for your SIEM. We'll attach our security pack.
[03:04] Jordan: Can you run multi-model routing? We sometimes route to a cheaper / smaller model for low-confidence queries.
[03:10] Sam (SE): Yes, our routing policy engine supports model tiers and fallback. You can route by latency SLO or cost thresholds. Also automatic fallback if a model is out of capacity.
[03:19] Priya: On the vLLM vs Dedicated tradeoff cost of running vLLM on our fleet looked cheaper, but we lost throughput and had memory fragmentation with 32k contexts. Any notes there?
[03:29] Sam (SE): vLLM can be cost-effective but requires tuning kernel selection, quantization, and continuous batching. Redwood's runtime includes optimized kernels and automated batching which helps at scale, and we expose quantization profiles you can test. That often brings latency and cost into the target.
[03:44] Jordan: What about model variants and tokenizer oddities we tried local TGI with the Falcon family and saw tokenization mismatch vs the hosted OpenAI endpoint, outputs diverged.
[03:53] Sam (SE): Right tokenizer vocab and byte-pair rules matter. We validate tokenizer parity during model onboarding. For the Falcon/TGI story, we have notes and a set of recommended tokenization configs we can share.
[04:03] Carlos: We'll need to run benchmarks against our prompt set. Can you support a Dedicated trial where we push our eval harness and also simulate nightly embedding batches?
[04:12] Alex (AE): Absolutely typical trial includes a small Dedicated pool, run your eval harness, and we'll collect perf/cost metrics. We'll also do a run with vLLM/TGI config to compare.
[04:21] Jordan: Good. On observability we need per-route latency and token-level cost. Can we get token breakdowns?
[04:27] Sam (SE): Yes, Redwood Console exposes token-level cost, per-route dashboards, and traces that map requests through the runtime, including cache hits.
[04:34] Priya: How do you handle KV cache warm-up for long conversations? We saw cold-starts kill latency.
[04:39] Sam (SE): We do prefix/KV caching and can pre-warm frequently used prefixes. Also our autoscaling can keep worker pools warm during spikes. We'll share best practices for cache keys and TTL.
[04:50] Carlos: Security: KMS integration with customer-managed keys is mandatory for us. We can't have Redwood-managed keys for certain datasets.
[04:58] Alex (AE): We support customer-managed KMS/HSM for Dedicated and Private. We'll include the integration guide in the security pack.
[05:05] Jordan: Any limitations on sequence lengths or quantization for our use case? We run up to 16k in some batches.
[05:12] Sam (SE): Our runtime supports long context models; for >8k we recommend specific kernel profiles and potentially GPU memory partitioning. Quantization works but you should run evals since some prompt families are more sensitive. We'll include quantization recommendations per model.
[05:26] Priya: Pricing generally are we looking at a committed monthly capacity or pay-as-you-go? Our expectation is reserved capacity for predictable unit economics.
[05:34] Alex (AE): Dedicated is typically reserved (monthly/annual commits) with burst capacity for spikes. Hosted remains usage-based. We'll send a pricing sheet with example workload scenarios.
[05:42] Jordan: For the POC, what telemetry do you need from us? Logs, prompts, eval harness, or synthetic load?
[05:49] Sam (SE): Eval harness and representative prompt sets are ideal. Also sample production traces for traffic shape. For security reasons you can obfuscate tokens; we only need structural similarity and failure cases.
[05:59] Carlos: Any enterprise compliance we should know about? SOC 2 and ISO?
[06:03] Alex (AE): We have SOC 2 Type II, and are working on ISO; we'll attach the current artifacts. Also we can sign data processing addendum and support contractual SLAs on Dedicated.
[06:13] Priya: Ok, next steps recap?
[06:16] Alex (AE): We'll: 1) Send security docs and SOC 2 report, 2) Share Dedicated pricing and capacity options, 3) Sam will send benchmark config and tokenizer compatibility notes, 4) Spin up trial Dedicated cluster (subject to paperwork) and schedule a run with your eval harness.
[06:30] Jordan: Sounds good. Aim for the trial spin-up in two weeks if possible.
[06:34] Alex (AE): We'll try to hit that. Thanks everyone.

End of transcript.
